account: This node is a pure design/decision node: its evidence is configuration/constraint framing, and the dossier explicitly carries "No source materials are provided" and "reasoning only." I can document the decision constraints as observed claims and the demanded deliverables, but the substantive thesis content (which thesis, which rejected candidate, the argument skeleton) is necessarily a reasoning artifact — it exists only as hypothesis/inference here, not as observable text in any source. I therefore report the framings (audience, register, length, stance, acceptance condition) with citations, and give the thesis-selection work only as hypotheses grounded in those shared facts, flagged for the writer/parent to settle. The single biggest gap is that nothing in the dossier can confirm a particular thesis; that is by design (the node rationale says it can be made by reasoning alone from the shared facts), so it is an expected reasoning boundary rather than an evidentiary omission.
assumptions: The intended research design treats thesis selection as reason-only, so hypotheses (not observed text) are the appropriate vehicle for the substantive claim.

boundary_findings.alternative_explanation: The gap is intended: decision:2 exists precisely so the thesis can be chosen by reasoning rather than by reading sources; this is an expected reasoning boundary, not a missing document.
boundary_findings.consequence_if_absorbed: A downstream/parent node would treat the proposal above as an observed fact of the dossier (e.g., as if 'AI shifts where kitsch lives' were a documented finding), silently converting a writer's reasoning hypothesis into evidence.
boundary_findings.narrative: The dossier states 'No source materials are provided' and 'reasoning only.' There is therefore no observable text from which a specific thesis can be evidenced; every proposed thesis, rejected alternative, and skeleton is a reasoning artifact rather than a documented fact. The node objective asks for a defended position the dossier cannot substantiate, by explicit design (rationale: decision can be made by reasoning alone from the shared facts).
boundary_findings.smallest_suspected_scope: This single route-root.01-thesis-design design node's outputs.

claims.statement: The node must deliver: one recommended thesis stated in a single sentence, at least one rejected alternative with a stated reason for rejection, and an ordered argument skeleton of moves each expressible in plain prose.

citations.excerpt: choose and defend a clear, nuanced thesis rather than produce a neutral survey

claims.statement: A neutral survey is explicitly out of scope; the writer must choose and defend a clear, nuanced thesis.
Total essay length must land within roughly 550-650 words (goal ~600).
The essay must be standalone/comprehensible without external context or companion materials, and must include a title.
The register is plain, accessible cultural-criticism prose; the suggested title is 'AI Art and Kitsch'; named theorists and citation apparatus are not required.
The audience is a general educated reader (decision:1).

A passable thesis must be more nuanced than 'AI art is kitsch' or 'AI art is not kitsch'; the objective suggests either a claim about what AI generation does to kitsch's logic or about where the kitsch actually resides (tool, output, market, or viewer).
No source materials are provided; the essay draws on the writer's own reasoning, which is confirmed as a deliberate design: 'It can be made by reasoning alone from the shared facts.'

citations.excerpt: a claim about what AI generation does to kitsch's logic, or about where the kitsch actually resides

counterevidence: Not observable in dossier; cannot be verified against any source.
claims.statement: Recommended working thesis (to be defended by writer): AI does not make art kitsch and does not spare it; instead AI shifts where kitsch lives — from qualities of the output or dispositions of the viewer to the logic of frictionless, intentionaless production itself, so that AI generation turns kitsch from an aesthetic verdict into a property of the tooling and its market.

counterevidence: The dossier does not itself record any rejected candidate; this is a constructed alternative.
claims.statement: Rejected candidate: 'AI art is kitsch' (plain assertion) — rejected because it is mechanical, fails the nuance requirement of decision:2, and makes no account of the specific transform AI performs on kitsch.

Rejected candidate: viewer/economy-only account locating kitsch wholly in the receiving market (e.g., 'users demand kitsch') — rejected because it under-specifies what the AI tool contributes and risks dissolving the category into general commodification, leaving no precise claim.

counterevidence: No source confirms any specific skeleton; must fit 550-650 words.
claims.statement: Working skeleton (4 moves, writer to confirm): (1) define kitsch's classic logic as sentiment without cost/friction and effect without conviction; (2) establish that AI generation is the maximal case of that logic, so output-level kitsch is redundant as a charge; (3) relocate the claim to the tool-market relation — the true kitsch is the market that manufactures stylized feeling on demand; (4) concede the strongest objection (human curation/authorship still matters) and hold the relocation.

counterevidence: The dossier contains no source material that can confirm or refute any specific thesis, rejected candidate, or argument skeleton; all substantive content exists only as reasoning hypothesis.
next_observation: Confirm which single-sentence thesis the writer will defend (kitsch located in tooling/market vs. in kitsch's frictionless logic), which one alternative is formally rejected and why, and the final ordered skeleton fitted to ~600 words.
unresolved: Which exact thesis single-sentence is chosen and which one alternative is the final 'rejected' candidate is left to the writer/parent; not determinable from the dossier.
Whether the kitsch-location view (tool/market) or the kitsch-behavioral-logic view wins is open.
